definition: Optimizing a policy against a reward rather than against reference outputs, and in both sources the more expensive option that is compared against a cheaper one rather than assumed. One applies its framework under both supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning, finds RL yields up to 12.58 points and the combination 17.04, and then declines it on cost grounds — naming substantially higher computational overhead against the more favourable trade of the supervised route. The other uses it to learn an optimal-stopping policy for pruning reasoning traces. The pairing is a useful corrective to how this archive usually reads RL results: the question is not only whether it works but whether the gain survives being priced.

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Recasts when-to-stop-reasoning as optimal stopping rather than classification, and proves that a fixed threshold on the probability of being correct can be arbitrarily far from optimal even when that probability is known exactly, because the decision needs the value of continuing and not the value of stopping.
evidence.title: OS-Pruner: Pruning Chains-of-Thought of Reasoning Models via Optimal Stopping

name: reinforcement learning
